items.quote: And when they had saddled the donkey for him, he mounted it and rode after the man of God.
items.contrast: The old prophet mounts the donkey, whereas his sons only saddle it for him.
items.reason: The singular “he” refers to the old prophet who requested the donkey; the sons are the plural “they” who saddle it.

items.quote: Azariah the priest with eighty other courageous priests of the Lord followed him in. They confronted King Uzziah
items.contrast: Uzziah is the person being followed, while Azariah and the eighty priests are the followers.
items.reason: The priests follow “him” and then confront that same person, explicitly identified as King Uzziah.

items.quote: Bring him back with you to your house so that he may eat bread and drink water.
items.contrast: The man of God is to eat and drink; the old prophet is instructed to bring him back.
items.reason: In the alleged angelic message, “him” and “he” refer to the man of God. However, “According to the claim” is an avoidably generic reference and should identify the old prophet’s alleged message.

items.quote: The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported within the palace.
items.contrast: The report concerns the news about the deserted camp, not the Aramean camp as a physical place.
items.reason: The pronoun “it” directly refers to “the news,” whose content is the preceding account of the camp.

items.quote: Listen to me, citizens of Shechem, so that God may listen to you.
items.contrast: God listening to the citizens is the intended result; anointing a king is part of the story Jotham begins afterward.
items.reason: The purpose clause “so that” explicitly states the result Jotham seeks from their listening.
